hints: If you first gathered all non-zero numbers at the front of nums (in order), what would be left to do with the rest of the array?

Write-pointer technique: copy every non-zero element to position k and advance k. Swapping nums[i] with nums[k] does the copy and pushes the zeros back at the same time. The function changes nums in place and returns nothing.

1. k = 0.
  2. For each i: if nums[i] != 0, swap nums[i] and nums[k], then k++.
  3. All zeros are now at the end.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Build a new array of the non-zero values, append the right number of zeros, then copy it back into nums.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: In place with one write pointer: swap each non-zero element into the next front slot.

explain: For nums = [0, 1, 0, 3, 12, 0]: 1 is swapped into slot 0, 3 into slot 1, 12 into slot 2, and the zeros drift to the back, leaving [1, 3, 12, 0, 0, 0]. The invariant is that nums[0..k-1] holds the non-zeros seen so far in their original order, and nums[k..i] holds only zeros. An array with no zeros just swaps each element with itself and stays the same.
recognize: "Move some elements to the end, keep the order of the rest, in place" → write pointer (stable partition).
